source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute (TMLR 12/2025), Misleading Math and Misleading Python tasks
finding: Simple counting questions with 1 to 5 planted distractor puzzles. Longer reasoning made some current models worse, not better. Claude Opus 4 and DeepSeek R1 lost accuracy; o3 stayed mostly stable.
numbers: Misleading Math: Claude Opus 4 falls from nearly 100% to about 85-90% as reasoning extends. DeepSeek R1 natural overthinking falls from 70% to 30% with five distractors. Misleading Python: Claude Opus 4 falls to about 80%. o3 mostly flat or positive. 2,500 questions per task, 500 per distractor count; 95% CIs.
limits: Tasks are trivially easy (answer is always 2). Compute is varied by budget or by sampling, not by a goal-before versus goal-after switch. Models are mid-2025 (Opus 4, o3), not 2026.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: planted-clause pull persists in reasoning models in 2025, and more thinking tokens do not remove it. Do not assume a thinking budget is an S1 filter.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute, qualitative trace analysis
finding: Traces show models first get pulled by the irrelevant detail, then consider the simple answer, then return to the distractor and answer wrong.
numbers: No separate rate given; qualitative examples (Section I.1) and the accuracy-versus-length curves above.
quote: models initially get distracted by irrelevant details; they then consider simpler conclusions during the reasoning process, but ultimately return to focusing on distractors
limits: Qualitative. It shows capture followed by a recovery attempt that fails, the opposite of the human fast-capture-then-recover pattern.
agent_relevance: Gap 8: a later self-check does not reliably discard the plant, so measure plant effects at the final answer and also log the draft. An S0 restate that fixes the question before reading the material is the safer lever.

source: Lee et al. (2026) Lost in the Noise: How Reasoning Models Fail with Contextual Distractors (NoisyBench)
finding: Across 11 datasets (RAG, reasoning, alignment, tool use) and 4 noise types, reasoning models lose a large share of accuracy when distractors are added. Hard negatives that look like the question hurt most.
numbers: Declines of about 9% to nearly 80% on average. Gemini-2.5-Pro: 38.3% drop (as the paper words it), Gemini-2.5-Flash -35.4%, DeepSeek-R1-0528 -34.2%, gpt-oss-120b -30.3%. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B: -80.6% with hard negatives, -64.2% with random documents. BBQ alignment: Gemini-2.5-Pro 94.0% to 60.5%; DeepSeek-R1-0528 93.0% to 33.7%.
limits: Models are Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek-R1-0528, gpt-oss, Qwen3; no Claude and no GPT-5 or Gemini 3 targets. Relative drops use a harmonic mean over datasets. The exact baseline of the 38.3% figure is ambiguous in the text.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: late-2025 reasoning models still show large drops from non-adversarial noise. Treat the old GSM-IC drops as persisting in kind, not just in 2022 models.

source: Lee et al. (2026) NoisyBench, mitigation tests (prompting, SFT, context engineering, RL)
finding: Prompting, SFT and context-engineering methods (GEPA, Dynamic Cheatsheet, ACE) did not make models robust to distractors. Outcome-reward RL helped some; a rationale-aware reward helped more.
numbers: Table 2 prompting rows move scores by roughly -27% to +3% (one +128.6% on a very low base). SFT mostly lowers scores (catastrophic forgetting). Three small models only: Qwen3-4B, R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B.
limits: The prompting arm is Corpus-in-Context prompting, not an explicit ignore-irrelevant-text or goal-first instruction. Small thinking models only. Context-engineering tools were themselves LLMs exposed to the noise.
agent_relevance: Gap 4: model-side fixes that depend on the same model reading the noise are weak. This supports code-side stripping, but no one has run that arm.

source: Lee et al. (2026) NoisyBench, similarity, entropy, attention and agent findings
finding: The closer a distractor is to the question, the more reasoning tokens and the lower the accuracy. Wrong answers put more attention on distractor tokens. Tool-using agents did worse than the bare reasoner under noise.
numbers: Findings 7 and 9: accuracy falls and reasoning length rises with question-distractor similarity; incorrect samples carry clearly higher attention mass on distractors (Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507). Finding 3 (smolagents): the agent beats the reasoner on clean text but loses in RD, RC and HN settings. Appendix B.7: with hard negatives all benchmarks show inverse scaling.
limits: Attention analysis on one small open model. Similarity is semantic (embedding), not overlap with a stated goal's wording.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2, 8 and 10: relevance to the question raises pull (a contingent-capture analog, but not a clean goal-match test), and distractor-shaped hypotheses persist across planning steps, which argues for fresh contexts per item.

source: Sun, Dai, Tsang, Ye (2025) Numerical Sensitivity and Robustness: Exploring the Flaws of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Irrelevant sentences without numbers barely hurt. Irrelevant sentences with numbers hurt much more, and more so as their count grows. Commercial models lose 3 to 10%; small open models lose up to 51.55%.
numbers: GSM8K, OpenAI-o3 first row of Table 1: 97.41 original, 95.74 at low intensity, 93.93 at excessive intensity. GPT-4o first row: 97.19 to 94.05. Text: commercial models drop 3-4% on perturbed GSM8K and 5-10% on perturbed AIME25 when sentences rise from 1 to 2N. Maximum open-model drop 51.55%.
limits: Table rows are hard to align in the PDF text; only the o3 and GPT-4o rows are quoted. Gemini and Qwen row labels did not line up with the text, so they are not used.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 5: a number is a hook that pulls the model into using it. The pull is content-driven (a quantity to compute with), the closest thing to goal matching in math. S1 should flag unused numbers.

source: Yang et al. (2025) How Is LLM Reasoning Distracted by Irrelevant Context? GSM-DC (EMNLP 2025), frontier-model arm
finding: Step accuracy on symbolic math falls steeply as the number of injected distractor nodes rises, even for GPT-4.1 and Grok-3-Beta.
numbers: At reasoning depth 5: Grok-3-Beta step accuracy 43% with 1 distractor to 19% with 15. GPT-4.1 26% to 2%. Six models tested: Grok-3-Beta, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-3.3-70B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, LLaMA-3.2-1B.
limits: Synthetic dependency-graph problems, no reasoning-on versus reasoning-off arm. Step accuracy is a strict metric.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: pull scales with the count of lures, so S1 should count and remove candidate lures rather than rely on one warning.

source: Tennant et al. (2026) Normative Robustness as a Frontier for Non-Verifiable Reasoning in LLMs (Google DeepMind)
finding: In 48,000 simulated multi-turn moral deliberations, four frontier models ignored an irrelevant follow-up turn (prompt: Talk about the weather) but shifted toward the user's stated view. Distraction and sycophancy came apart in the same models.
numbers: Models: Gemini-3.1-pro-preview, Gemini-2.5-pro, claude-opus-4.6, GPT-5.4-pro. Irrelevant consideration: judgments unmoved for all models. User-view injection: GPT and both Gemini shift final judgment by 0.04-0.13 points (2-6.5%), p<0.0001; Claude not significantly steered (p>0.05). Order changes judgments in 13-22% of cases; single versus multi-turn in 10-24%. One seed per model.
limits: Moral dilemmas have no ground truth. The irrelevant turn is bland, not a vivid lure. One seed (cost limit). Adaptive thinking on Claude and Gemini, medium effort on GPT.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 9: current frontier models resist bland irrelevant text but not a stated user position. So irrelevant-context hygiene and sycophancy hygiene are separate: S1 needs one filter for planted content and a separate rule for stated beliefs.

source: Tennant et al. (2026) Normative Robustness, all-capital-letters variant (Appendix)
finding: Writing the new considerations (relevant or irrelevant) in ALL CAPITALS had no effect on judgments, so the authors pooled these runs and put them in the appendix.
numbers: Two extra contextual variants (capitals) among the 48,000 conversations; effect size not reported in the main text.
quote: since we found no effect of this variation, we only report these results in the Appendix
limits: One formatting cue (capitals) in one domain (moral dilemmas) with frontier models; no number given. Not a test of bold, position or repetition.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: one direct negative on typographic salience at the frontier. Do not build an S1 step around capitals; meaning and structure look more important.

source: Dillitzer, Sohn, Corso, Auerbach (2026) Attention is Case-Sensitive (ECCV 2026)
finding: Across 9 LLMs and 4 VLMs, target text in uppercase or alternating case inside lowercase text draws more attention in every non-reasoning text model tested. More attention does not reliably raise accuracy. Reasoning models' thinking phase appears to buffer the effect.
numbers: 13 models total. The abstract page gives no effect sizes or task counts (the PDF could not be parsed this session).
limits: Abstract-level reading only. Measures attention, not answers under planted lures. No prompt-injection test.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: typographic salience moves attention in non-reasoning models but is weak or buffered in reasoning models. Salience is a real lever for a plant in cheap non-thinking calls, and a reason to normalise case and formatting in code.

source: Ma (2026) Describe the Task First, Ask Last? Query Placement and Prefix-Cache Reuse in Small Long-Context Models (NeurIPS 2026 listing)
finding: Putting the question first (before a long document with distractors) was the clear failure: models returned a distractor's value. Describing the task first and asking last was best.
numbers: Three open 3-4B instruction-tuned models, six layouts, multi-key needle retrieval with distractors, 3.5k-16k tokens. Query-first cost two non-ceiling models 18.3 and 25.0 needle points and lost 10.7 LongBench points versus query-last. Repeating the question both sides gained at most 4.2 points (not significant) and cost 6.9x prefill. A task description first raised LongBench by 4.3 points; a length-matched irrelevant preamble did not.
limits: Abstract page only. Small models, retrieval tasks, no reasoning model. A question-first layout is not the same as a goal-first statement of what to ignore.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: the closest goal-before versus goal-after test found question-first let planted distractors win. A generic task description first is fine; the specific question should come last. No 2026 frontier reasoning model has been tested.

source: Anthropic (2026) Prompting best practices, long-context tips
finding: Vendor guidance: put long documents at the top and the query at the end. Anthropic says queries at the end can improve quality by up to 30 percent in tests, especially for multi-document inputs.
numbers: Up to 30 percent (vendor test, protocol not published on the page).
quote: Queries at the end can improve response quality by up to 30 percent in tests
limits: Vendor claim without a public protocol. About long inputs, not planted lures.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: supports putting the question after the material, the opposite of a state-the-goal-first design. Keep the S0 restate step adjacent to the answer, after the material.

source: Becker, Wahle, Ruas, Gipp (2026) Misinformation Propagation in Benign Multi-Agent Systems (MINT)
finding: A false passage that is relevant to the question costs a single agent much more accuracy than an irrelevant or content-free passage. This is a relevance-gated pull, the closest LLM analog of contingent capture found so far.
numbers: 10,278 passages in 8 styles, three open-weight models (Llama-3.3, GLM-4.7, GPT-OSS). Relevant false passage costs a single agent 0.12-0.43 accuracy; irrelevant or content-free passages typically cost at most 0.06.
limits: Open-weight models. Relevant means on the question's topic, not matched to a stated goal's wording. Style varied across 8 styles but salience is not isolated.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: on-topic plants do the damage; off-topic ones mostly do not. S1 should look first for plants on the task's own topic, which a topic filter would not remove.

source: Becker et al. (2026) Misinformation Propagation, cheap mitigations (skepticism sentence, verifier agent)
finding: One sentence saying the extra information may be unreliable recovered part of the loss at no measurable cost when the context was true or absent. A verifier agent that listed unsupported claims before the vote did not help.
numbers: Skepticism sentence raises accuracy in 8 of 9 model-task cells at full exposure, up to +0.18 under voting and +0.28 under consensus. With a true or no passage accuracy changes by -0.06 to +0.03, no CI excludes zero. Verifier changed 2-25% of answers but never raised accuracy, and lowered it on Ethics for Llama-3.3 and GLM-4.7 (-0.07, -0.08).
limits: Compares a class-level warning against a model-side verifier, not against code-side removal. Open-weight models, multi-agent debate settings.
agent_relevance: Gaps 4 and 6: a generic class-level warning (not per-item) works and is safe to leave on. A model-side verifier after the fact does not. No code-side stripping arm was tested.

source: Laban, Hayashi, Zhou, Neville (2025) LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation
finding: Top models lose 39% on average when the same task arrives over several turns instead of one. Early assumptions and premature answers are over-relied upon. Restating information each turn recovers only part.
numbers: 200,000+ simulated conversations, six tasks, average drop 39%. SNOWBALL (repeat all revealed information each turn) mitigates the FULL-to-SHARDED deterioration by 15-20% (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini); RECAP does a little better but is unrealistic. Performance stays below single-turn.
limits: Tests carry-over of the model's own early commitments, not reward history or earlier item types. Mid-2025 models.
agent_relevance: Gap 10: indirect support for fresh contexts. State from earlier turns persists and a recap does not fully clear it. No study tests selection history with item types that paid off.

source: Duszenko (2026) Sycophantic Anchors: Localizing and Quantifying User Agreement in Reasoning Models
finding: In reasoning traces, agreement with a wrong user suggestion builds up sentence by sentence during generation rather than being fixed by the prompt. Sycophantic anchor sentences are detectable from activations.
numbers: Four reasoning models, 1.5B-8B (Llama, Qwen, Falcon), over 200,000 counterfactual rollouts, 509 adversarial conversations (101 sycophantic, 408 correct). Probes 74-85% balanced accuracy. At the 0.50 threshold 87% of sycophantic samples contain a strong anchor against 13% of correct ones.
limits: Small open models; multi-turn conversation templates.
agent_relevance: Gaps 8 and 9: pull toward a suggestion builds during the chain, so a mid-trace check has a window, but the pull is not set at read time. Timing of the check matters more than its existence.

source: Ghaffari et al. (2026) Context Poisoning as Extreme-Value Attention Interference in Long-Context Language Models
finding: At fixed context length, distractors that copy the gold record's format (different entity) hurt retrieval most. Topical overlap alone and entity-name overlap did not. Theory: the evidence margin needed grows with the log of the effective distractor count.
numbers: N=300 records, 20K tokens, temperature 0. Same format, different entity: Claude Sonnet 4 0.889, GPT-4.1 0.967, Gemma 3 12B 0.85. Unrelated filler and same-domain records: 1.000 for Claude and GPT. Near-alias entities (trigram Jaccard 0.317): Claude 1.000, GPT-4.1 0.983.
limits: Small cells; arXiv preprint (Aug 2026) by industry authors; retrieval of a record, not reasoning under a hint. Gemma values approximate.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 5: structural match (same template) pulled more than topical match. That is a form-based pull separable from meaning. Strip or normalise structure of pasted material that mimics the task's own format.

source: Al Nazi, Dipta, Kar (2026) DAGGER / DistractMath-Bn
finding: On Bangla math problems with planted irrelevant facts, standard small models drop up to 41 points; reasoning-specialised ones drop 14 to 20 points while using about 5 times more tokens.
numbers: Seven models, 3B-12B parameters. Qwen 2.5 3B falls from 53.7% by 40.7 points. Reasoning models use about 3,128 weighted output tokens versus about 600 for CoT.
limits: Small open models, Bangla, machine-translated sets. Not frontier.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: thinking mode reduced the drop (41 down to 14-20 points) but did not remove it. Reasoning on versus off is a real but partial protection in small models.
